Thought: Let me analyze each salt to determine its color in aqueous solution:

A. CuSO4 (Copper(II) sulfate): This forms a blue aqueous solution due to the presence of Cu²⁺ ions. The hydrated form [Cu(H₂O)₆]²⁺ gives a characteristic blue color.

B. K2CrO4 (Potassium chromate): This forms a yellow aqueous solution due to the CrO₄²⁻ ions, which are yellow in color.

C. NaClO4 (Sodium perchlorate): Both Na⁺ and ClO₄⁻ ions are colorless in aqueous solution. Na⁺ is a Group 1 metal ion (colorless), and perchlorate ions do not absorb visible light.

D. Ni(NO3)2 (Nickel(II) nitrate): This forms a green aqueous solution due to the Ni²⁺ ions, which typically give a green color in aqueous solution.

Among these options, only NaClO4 would yield a colorless aqueous solution because both its constituent ions (Na⁺ and ClO₄⁻) are colorless in water.
Final Answer: [ANSWER]C[/ANSWER]
